raw_graphql_pull_request.body: Route the HIP/gfx950 self-attention prepare through sglang's own fused_qk_gemma_rmsnorm_rope_gate (one Triton launch) instead of fused_qk_gemma_rmsnorm_with_gate + rotary_emb (two launches), matching the CUDA path. Defensive import under `_use_aiter and _is_gfx95` with an internal A/B toggle (_hip_fused_prep_enabled); falls back to the 2-kernel path if the kernel cannot import on ROCm Triton. Unpack the fused-AR (bf16, fp8, scale) tuple in forward_prepare_cuda_fused before qkv_proj, like its sibling prepare methods (required now that the HIP path reaches it with --enable-aiter-allreduce-fusion). Make the kernel importable on ROCm: guard the libdevice import and disable Hopper PDL on HIP. ## Motivation In Qwen3.5's full-attention layers, there is a "prepare" step that builds the query, key, and gate before attention runs. On gfx950 (MI355X) this step uses **two** GPU kernels: the first does QK RMSNorm and splits out the gate, and the second applies RoPE. On NVIDIA/CUDA, the same work is already done by a **single** kernel, `fused_qk_gemma_rmsnorm_rope_gate`. So on gfx950 we launch one extra kernel on every full-attention layer (15 of the 60 layers), on every decode step. That extra launch costs time for no real benefit. This PR turns on the single-kernel path on gfx950, so the prepare step uses **1 kernel instead of 2**. The kernel is written in Triton (not CUDA C++), and it already handles partial RoPE, interleaved mRoPE, and the Gemma `+1` norm, so it produces the same result as before for Qwen3.5. ## Modifications - On gfx950, send the prepare step through the single fused kernel instead of the two-kernel path. We import the kernel only when it is available (`_use_aiter and _is_gfx95`). If it cannot be imported on the installed Triton, the code falls back to the old two-kernel path, so nothing breaks. A simple on/off switch, `_hip_fused_prep_enabled` (no new environment variable), lets you compare the new path against the old one. - When all-reduce fusion is on (`--enable-aiter-allreduce-fusion`), the input arrives as a `(bf16, fp8, scale)` tuple. We now unpack that tuple before calling `qkv_proj`, the same way the other two prepare functions already do. This does nothing on CUDA. - Let the kernel import on ROCm. The `libdevice` import is only needed for an option that is off by default, so we wrap it in a `try/except`. We also turn off Hopper PDL on AMD, since AMD GPUs do not have it. - No change on CUDA or on non-gfx950 GPUs. ## Accuracy Tests gsm8k (5-shot), `amd/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4-AttnFP8-V2`, TP=2, gfx950. The scores match within the margin of error: | Build | flexible-extract | strict-match | |---|---|---| | before (2 kernels) | 0.9735 ± 0.0044 | 0.9735 ± 0.0044 | | this PR (1 kernel) | 0.9750 ± 0.0043 | 0.9757 ± 0.0042 | ## Speed Tests and Profiling Online serving, `amd/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4-AttnFP8-V2`, TP=2, input 8192 / output 1024, gfx950 (MI355X). Throughput is per-GPU tokens/s (higher is better). TPOT is the median time per output token during decode (lower is better). | Concurrency | Throughput before | Throughput this PR | Change | TPOT before (ms) | TPOT this PR (ms) | Change | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 4 | 2381.68 | 2404.15 | +0.9% | 7.07 | 7.00 | −1.0% | | 8 | 3572.63 | 3600.54 | +0.8% | 9.68 | 9.60 | −0.8% | | 16 | 4748.49 | 4783.82 | +0.7% | 14.54 | 14.37 | −1.2% | | 32 | 5900.10 | 5922.35 | +0.4% | 23.55 | 23.55 | ~0% | | 64 | 7892.26 | 7893.67 | +0.0% | 35.85 | 35.79 | −0.2% | | 128 | 9665.86 | 9778.12 | +1.2% | 58.10 | 57.49 | −1.1% | The change is small but steady: a little faster and never slower, with accuracy unchanged. The gain is small because the prepare step is only a small part of each decode step. ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. +# Single-launch fused QK-GemmaRMSNorm + partial-RoPE + gate-deinterleave kernel.

+# regression. The kernel's only NVIDIA-specific bits (libdevice FMA, Hopper PDL)
+# are optional and default-off.
+_HIP_FUSED_PREP_AVAILABLE = False

 import triton

-from triton.language.extra.cuda import libdevice

+try:
+    from triton.language.extra.cuda import libdevice
+except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
+    # ROCm / non-CUDA Triton may not ship the CUDA libdevice shim. libdevice is
+    # only dereferenced under EXPLICIT_ROPE_FMA (constexpr, default False), which
+    # Triton prunes, so a None placeholder keeps the kernel importable on gfx950.
+    libdevice = None
 
 
 def _pdl_supported() -> bool:
     """Check if Programmatic Dependent Launch is supported (NVIDIA SM >= 90)."""
     if not torch.cuda.is_available():
         return False
+    if getattr(torch.version, "hip", None) is not None:
+        # PDL (gdc_launch_dependents) is NVIDIA Hopper+ only; ROCm has no equivalent.
+        return False
     try:
         major, _ = torch.cuda.get_device_capability()
         return major >= 9
